title: What Is a Living Trust and Do You Really Need One?
bigPicture: A living trust is a paper that says who gets your stuff after you die, and it can skip the court process.
whatYouNeedToKnow: It holds your money, house, and things while you are alive.
You can change it or cancel it anytime you want.
It helps your family avoid a long court process after you die.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Thinking a trust covers everything if you don't put your house and bank accounts into it.
Forgetting to name a backup person in charge if your first choice can't serve.
actionSteps: List what you own and decide who gets each item.
Talk to an estate lawyer to make the trust fit your state rules.
